drafted_from: tool:arrange-videos's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json (its argv builds a split edit for tools/media-composition/do-work/render-an-edit.mjs), and that script run on two synthetic clips
start_here: Say to your AI: "Put my swing video next to the pro's video, side by side, for 4 seconds." It runs tool:arrange-videos and saves the combined video in your files.
no_lists_because: It makes a new video in your files from the video you name and keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find the identities of two to nine videos in your files (1f: then 64 hex each).

2. Say "Arrange these videos side by side" with the videos. Optional: layout ("h" side by side, default; "v" stacked; "grid"), seconds (how long to play), width and height of the output (default 1920 by 1080).

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:arrange-videos. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result (duration_seconds, width, height, bytes) and files.video, the arranged video in your files; the sound of the videos is mixed.

worked_examples.title: Two clips side by side for 4 seconds
worked_examples.ask: Put these two videos side by side for 4 seconds.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/render-an-edit.mjs and run on a 7 second clip and a 26 second clip with layout h, seconds 4, width 640, height 180
